High Quality Clean Ltd respects your privacy and aims to handle personal information transparently, securely and only for appropriate purposes.
This Privacy Policy explains how we collect and use personal information when you:

items: send photographs, video or property information;
work with us as a commercial or property client;

privacy.text: 1. Who We Are
High Quality Clean Ltd
Registered in England and Wales
Company number: [CONFIRM BEFORE PUBLICATION]
Registered office: [CONFIRM BEFORE PUBLICATION]
Website: highqualityclean.co.uk
Privacy contact: [CONFIRM PRIVACY EMAIL]
For the purposes of UK data protection law, High Quality Clean Ltd is normally the data controller for the personal information described in this policy.
2. Information We May Collect
Identity and contact information
Property and service information
Photographs, video and supporting material
Where necessary to assess or deliver a service, you may provide property photographs, short videos, floor plans, inventories, site information or supporting documents.
These materials may incidentally contain personal belongings or other personal information. Please avoid sending information that is not necessary for the cleaning requirement.
Enquiry, quotation and booking information
Payment and financial information
Payments may be processed through third-party payment providers. HQC may receive transaction information such as amount, payment status, transaction reference and refund status.
HQC does not need to store full payment-card details where those are handled directly by the payment provider.
Communications
Website and technical information

Depending on your choices and the technology in use, this may include IP address, device/browser information, pages visited, referral source, campaign parameters, website interactions, cookie identifiers and analytics information.
3. Information Provided by Another Person or Organisation
HQC may sometimes receive personal information about you from another authorised person or organisation, for example:
We may use that information where reasonably necessary to arrange, quote, access or deliver the relevant service.
Where data-protection law requires us to provide privacy information directly to you, we will do so within the applicable period unless a lawful exception applies.
People or organisations providing another person's information to HQC should only provide information they are authorised to share and that is reasonably necessary for the service.
4. Why We Use Personal Information
To respond to enquiries and prepare quotations
We use information to understand your requirement, communicate with you and take steps towards a possible contract.
Typical lawful basis: steps at your request before entering into a contract.
To manage bookings and provide services
Typical lawful basis: performance of a contract.
To operate customer and commercial relationships
We may maintain records of previous instructions, quotations, property requirements, communications and client relationships to support continuity, administration and service management.
Typical lawful basis: contract and/or legitimate interests, depending on the circumstances.
To meet legal, tax and accounting obligations
We keep appropriate transaction, invoice and business records where required.
Typical lawful basis: legal obligation.
To protect HQC, clients and others
Typical lawful basis: legitimate interests and, where applicable, legal obligations.
To improve our website and services
Subject to applicable consent requirements, analytics may help us understand how people use the site, which pages help clients, where enquiries come from and where website performance can improve.
Marketing
Where permitted, we may send occasional service updates, offers or relevant news.
Where consent is required, marketing consent will be requested separately from the service enquiry. You can unsubscribe from marketing at any time.
5. Information We Need to Deliver the Service
Some information is necessary for HQC to provide a quotation, confirm the booking, obtain access, deliver the agreed service or meet legal and financial obligations.
If necessary information is not supplied, we may be unable to quote, book or safely provide the service.
6. Who We May Share Information With
We may use trusted service providers to support our operations.
Depending on the service and systems in use, these can include providers of:
HQC currently uses systems which may include:

items: GoHighLevel for CRM and enquiry management;
Launch27/Automaid for applicable booking and scheduling functions;

privacy.text: Where cleaners, subcontractors or specialists need client information to deliver the authorised service, they should receive only the information reasonably necessary for that purpose.
We do not sell personal information to advertisers.
7. International Transfers
Some technology providers may process or store information outside the United Kingdom.
Where personal information is transferred internationally, HQC will use the relevant lawful transfer mechanism or rely on the applicable safeguards where required.
8. How Long We Keep Information
HQC applies the storage-limitation principle: information should not be kept for longer than is reasonably necessary for the purpose for which it is held.

The following is the approved HQC retention schedule for the customer-facing systems, subject to any legal requirement, active dispute, fraud prevention need or other documented reason to retain information longer.
Retention periods may be suspended where information is subject to a legal hold, active complaint, fraud investigation, regulatory requirement or live dispute.
Recruitment, worker and subcontractor records are governed separately and are not intended to be covered by the customer-data periods above.
9. Cookies and Similar Technologies
Strictly necessary technologies
Required for essential website functionality, security or a service you request.
Analytics technologies
Used to understand website performance and visitor interaction.
Advertising or campaign technologies
Used, where enabled and consented to, to understand campaign effectiveness or support advertising.
Non-essential cookies or similar technologies should not be activated until the applicable consent has been obtained. Users should have a practical way to change their choices.
Link: Manage Cookie Preferences
10. Marketing Preferences
Submitting a quotation or contact form does not automatically mean you have agreed to marketing.
Where HQC asks for marketing permission:

items: it should be clearly distinguishable from the service enquiry;
you can withdraw consent or unsubscribe.

privacy.text: Service communications required to manage your enquiry or booking are different from promotional marketing.
11. Security

HQC uses reasonable technical and organisational measures intended to protect personal information. These may include access controls, secure accounts, restricted staff access, appropriate service-provider controls, data minimisation and system/process safeguards.
No internet or information system can be guaranteed to be completely secure.
12. Your Data Protection Rights
Depending on the circumstances and lawful basis, you may have rights including:

items: withdrawal of consent where processing relies on consent.

privacy.text: To make a request, contact: [PRIVACY EMAIL]
We may need to verify your identity before responding.
13. Complaints About Data Protection
If you have a concern, please contact HQC first so we can try to address it.
You also have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office.
Information Commissioner's Office - ico.org.uk
14. Third-Party Websites
The HQC website may link to external services or websites. Those organisations operate under their own privacy policies and are responsible for their own processing.
15. Changes to This Privacy Policy
We may update this policy where our services, technology, processors, law or regulatory guidance change.
The current version will be published on the website with its review date.

These Terms explain the basis on which High Quality Clean Ltd supplies cleaning services.
Nothing in these Terms is intended to remove or restrict consumer rights that cannot legally be excluded.
1. Company and Definitions
High Quality Clean Ltd - Registered in England and Wales.
In these Terms:

items: HQC, we, us, our means High Quality Clean Ltd.
Client, you, your means the person or organisation buying or instructing the service.
Service means the cleaning or related service agreed with HQC.
Booking means a service that HQC has expressly confirmed.
Quotation means HQC's proposed scope and price.
Essential Clean™ means HQC's maintenance-cleaning route for suitable homes.
Quoted Service means a service requiring manual quotation or assessment.
Commercial Service means a service supplied principally for business, property-management or organisational purposes.

terms.text: 2. Service Selection and Scope
HQC's services are defined according to the required outcome.

Before work begins, the applicable information may identify service, property/site, included areas, selected extras, exclusions, assumptions, access, timing, frequency, specialist requirements and quotation or booking price.
The agreed service does not automatically include every possible cleaning task.
3. Information Supplied by the Client

You must provide information that is reasonably accurate and complete. This may include property condition, property size, contents, service requirement, access, parking, pets, sensitive or valuable items, construction activity, specialist finishes, known hazards and deadline.
HQC may rely on this information when pricing and planning the service.
If the actual circumstances differ materially, the service, labour, price or timing may need to change.
4. Quotations

items: a quotation covers only the stated scope;
additional work is not automatically included;
quotations remain subject to availability until booking is confirmed;
a quotation may have an expiry date.

terms.text: Where new information materially changes the requirement, HQC may issue a revised quotation.
5. Booking Confirmation
An enquiry or quotation request is not a confirmed booking.

A booking becomes confirmed only when HQC completes the applicable confirmation process, which may include acceptance of a quotation, required booking information, deposit or payment where applicable, written confirmation from HQC or successful online booking confirmation.
Do not rely on a requested date as reserved until HQC confirms it.
6. Pricing and VAT
Prices will be stated as excluding VAT, including VAT or with VAT separately shown, as applicable.
HQC pricing may consider scope, labour, property/site condition, rooms and bathrooms, access, floors, contents, frequency, equipment, specialist work, direct service costs and complexity.
Internal HQC margin calculations and labour-cost formulas do not form part of the client contract unless expressly stated.
7. Payment
Payment timing depends on the service and may include payment at booking, deposit, payment before service, payment on completion, recurring card payment or invoicing under agreed commercial terms.
The applicable quotation, booking confirmation or commercial proposal will state the payment requirement.
HQC may withhold confirmation or suspend future work where amounts that are properly due remain unpaid, subject to applicable law and contract terms.
8. Essential Clean™ Recurring Introductory Offer
The offer:

items: applies only to eligible new weekly or fortnightly Essential Clean™ arrangements;
applies to the first eligible clean only;
does not apply to one-off Essential Clean™ bookings;
does not apply to other HQC services;
is subject to property suitability and service availability.

terms.text: When the minimum commitment begins
The minimum commitment begins on the date of the first discounted recurring Essential Clean™ and runs for three calendar months.
The agreed weekly or fortnightly frequency is expected to continue during that period, subject to reasonable rescheduling.
Rescheduled or skipped visits
Rescheduling an individual visit does not end the recurring arrangement.

Where a client repeatedly cancels or suspends enough visits to materially defeat the agreed recurring arrangement, HQC may review the pattern and, after considering the circumstances, treat the arrangement as having ended early.
Early termination and introductory discount balance

Where a client receives the introductory discount and ends the qualifying recurring arrangement before completing the agreed minimum term, HQC may charge the discount balance that would have been payable on the first clean without the introductory discount, subject to statutory rights and the fairness requirements applicable to the contract.
The discount balance is intended to reverse the conditional introductory discount, not impose an unrelated penalty.
Notice given before the end of the minimum term

A client may give notice during the three-month minimum term for the recurring arrangement to end when the minimum term is completed. The client does not need to wait until the final day of the minimum term before giving notice.
After the minimum commitment
After the three-month minimum term, the recurring arrangement continues until ended on one normal service cycle's notice:
If HQC ends the recurring arrangement
Where HQC chooses to end the recurring arrangement for its own operational reasons, the introductory discount balance will not normally be charged merely because HQC ended the service.
A different position may apply where termination follows a material client breach and the contract lawfully provides for that outcome.
9. Commercial and Other Recurring Agreements
A commercial or recurring service may have a minimum term, notice period, mobilisation requirements, agreed frequencies and price-review provisions.
These apply only where stated in the applicable proposal or agreement.
There is no blanket 12-month minimum term simply because a service is recurring.
10. Consumer Statutory Cancellation Rights
Where a consumer enters into a qualifying distance or off-premises service contract, statutory cancellation rights may apply.
These statutory rights operate separately from HQC's ordinary appointment-cancellation policy below.
Where a consumer asks HQC to begin providing a service during an applicable statutory cancellation period, HQC may require the consumer's express request and any acknowledgement required by law.
Where permitted by law, a consumer who later cancels after performance has begun may be required to pay a proportionate amount for services already supplied.
Nothing in the HQC appointment-cancellation matrix overrides mandatory consumer rights.
11. HQC Appointment Cancellation & Rescheduling Matrix

The matrix below is HQC's normal operational policy for appointments. Any amount charged must remain subject to applicable consumer law and must not exceed HQC's reasonably incurred loss resulting from the cancellation, taking account of costs saved and capacity successfully reallocated.

terms.text: Exceptional circumstances and management discretion
HQC may waive or reduce a cancellation charge where exceptional circumstances justify doing so. Material waivers should be recorded so the policy is applied consistently.
Repeated rescheduling

Where repeated free rescheduling materially prevents HQC from operating the booking as agreed, HQC may ask the client to confirm a new booking rather than continue moving the same appointment indefinitely.
12. HQC Cancellation or Material Rescheduling
If HQC cancels an appointment before attendance, the client will not be charged an HQC cancellation fee for that appointment.
Where the client has prepaid for the affected service, the client may normally choose between:

items: a credit for the affected service;
a refund of the applicable prepaid amount.

terms.text: If HQC materially changes an agreed date or delivery arrangement and the alternative is not reasonably acceptable to the client, the applicable prepaid amount for the affected service should be refunded, subject to any separate lawful agreement.
Nothing in this section limits any statutory remedy that applies.
13. Project and Assessment-Led Cancellation Terms
Larger or assessment-led services may require HQC to reserve several cleaners, subcontractors, equipment, project-management time or other direct resources.
Examples can include:

items: work requiring specialist subcontractors or equipment.

terms.text: A quotation may therefore include project-specific cancellation or deposit terms where those terms are clearly provided before the contract is made.
Any cancellation amount must be reasonable and should reflect losses directly arising from the cancellation, taking account of costs HQC avoids and reasonable steps taken to reduce the loss.
Where valid project-specific terms apply, they take precedence over the standard appointment matrix for that project, subject to applicable law.
14. Access and Aborted Visits

The Client is responsible for providing the access arrangements agreed with HQC, which may include keys, concierge, access codes, authorised representatives, parking/loading arrangements and alarm instructions.

If the team cannot gain access, or cannot safely proceed for reasons outside HQC's control, the visit may be delayed, shortened, rescheduled or treated as an aborted attendance under the cancellation matrix.
Where access is delayed by the client, the service does not automatically extend beyond the scheduled working window. Additional labour is subject to team availability and agreement.
15. Safe Working Conditions
The Client must disclose relevant known conditions that could affect safe delivery.

HQC may pause or refuse work where there are dangerous conditions, uncontrolled hazards, unsafe access, aggressive animals, hazardous materials, sharps, suspected asbestos or conditions requiring competence HQC does not hold.
16. Property Condition and Variations

If the property or site materially differs from the information supplied, HQC may pause the work, explain the difference, offer revised scope, quote additional labour, recommend another service, arrange specialist support or decline work that cannot safely or responsibly continue.
Additional work should not be assumed to be included without agreement.
17. Specialist and Sensitive Items
Clients should disclose fragile items, unusually valuable items, specialist surfaces, sensitive materials, known defects and items requiring manufacturer-specific treatment.
Where there is uncertainty about a surface or item, HQC may avoid treatment until an appropriate method can be confirmed.
18. Appliances, Windows, Carpets and Other Add-Ons
Specialist or additional services are included only where expressly selected or quoted.
19. End of Tenancy™
HQC agrees a cleaning scope designed to prepare the relevant property areas for handover.
HQC does not guarantee return of a deposit, inventory approval, landlord approval, agent approval or removal of permanent wear or damage.
Third-party decisions remain outside HQC's control.
20. Post-Construction™
The property or work area should be sufficiently ready for cleaning.
If dust-producing works, contractors or snagging continue, HQC cannot guarantee that cleaned areas will remain free from further residue.
Recontamination or additional contractor activity may require further paid work.
21. Recurring and Commercial Services
Recurring programmes may distinguish between routine work, periodic work, specialist work and variations.
Tasks outside the agreed service profile are not automatically absorbed into recurring labour.
22. Team Allocation and Subcontractors
HQC may use employees, self-employed cleaning professionals, subcontractors or specialist providers where appropriate to the agreed service.
HQC does not guarantee that the same individual cleaner will attend every visit unless expressly agreed.
23. Service Timing
HQC will aim to attend and complete work within the agreed arrangements.
Exact completion times may be affected by condition, access, traffic, previous jobs, contractor activity, unexpected site conditions or events beyond reasonable control.
Where a fixed completion deadline is critical, it must be made clear before booking and expressly agreed.
24. Quality, Complaints and Remedial Action
If you believe the agreed service has not been delivered appropriately, notify HQC as soon as reasonably practicable.
Please provide booking details, affected area, description and photographs where useful and appropriate.
HQC will consider the agreed scope, property condition, available evidence, service records and appropriate corrective action.
An operational request to report an issue promptly does not remove any statutory rights or legal time limit.
25. Results and Limitations

Professional cleaning can improve cleanliness and presentation, but HQC cannot guarantee removal of permanent stains, wear, damage, discolouration, etching, deterioration, defects or contamination beyond the agreed cleaning method.
HQC will not deliberately use a method likely to damage a surface merely to pursue an unrealistic result.
26. Damage and Pre-Existing Conditions
Where damage is reported, HQC will investigate the circumstances.
Clients should notify HQC promptly and preserve relevant evidence.
Nothing in these Terms excludes or limits liability where doing so would be unlawful.
27. Insurance
HQC maintains insurance appropriate to its operations. Specific insurance details can be provided where reasonably required for commercial qualification.
28. Force Majeure and Events Beyond Reasonable Control
Neither party should be treated as having failed to perform an obligation where performance is prevented by an event genuinely beyond reasonable control, subject to applicable law.
HQC will communicate material disruption and seek a reasonable alternative where possible.
29. Personal Information
Personal information is handled in accordance with the HQC Privacy Policy.
Link: Privacy Policy
30. Intellectual Property
HQC names, written materials, service architecture and relevant branded service names remain the property of their respective owner.
Clients may not represent themselves as HQC or reproduce proprietary HQC materials for commercial use without permission.
31. Changes to These Terms
The Terms applicable to a booking are those incorporated into the agreement when the relevant contract is made, together with any subsequent change expressly agreed where required.
Publishing updated website Terms does not retrospectively rewrite an existing contract where the law requires agreement.
32. Governing Law
These Terms are governed by the law of England and Wales.
Consumer clients retain any mandatory rights regarding jurisdiction that cannot lawfully be restricted.
